note: Track singing-modes (voice-melodies), step 6: Locrian over a drone, heard against Phrygian (a Scale choice: only the 5th moves), its home chord 1 ♭3 ♭5 in three keys, then a made-up tune that ends every phrase on 1. Missing: a Locrian progression on backing-track (it has a vamp for every other mode), so the tune is made up over the drone, not over a band.

exercise.title: Locrian over a drone
exercise.why: Locrian is Phrygian with one more note lowered, the ♭5, so singing the same five notes in both scales over one drone lets you hear the one note that moves.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing the first five notes of the scale up from the low {{1}} and back down, on "oo". The ringed note is {{b5}}, a half step above {{4}}.
Then sing the same five notes in Phrygian. Use the Scale selector below to change the scale, then press Start exercise to start the drone again.
When you change the scale, only the ringed note moves: it is {{5}} in Phrygian and {{b5}} in Locrian.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. These three notes are the chord on {{1}} in Locrian. Sing {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{b5}} up and back down, on "oo". Then leap from the low {{1}} straight up to {{b5}} and back.
Once the leap lands without a slide, sing it in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Start exercise to start the drone there.
When you change the key, the drone moves and the chord is still {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{b5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Make up a short tune from the whole scale, and sing it on "la". Pass through {{b5}} in every phrase, and end every phrase on {{1}}, so your ear keeps the drone as home.
If a phrase ends on another note and sounds finished there, sing its last two notes again and add {{1}}.
